{{Quote|I think I have the powers you seek.|Nichos Marr, to Luke Skywalker, upon arriving on Yavin 4|<ref name="COJ" />}}
'''Nichos Marr''', a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]], was a [[Jedi Initiate/Legends|Jedi trainee]] at the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] during the last days of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. With the emergence of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and the beginning of the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], Marr was among a [[Children of the Jedi|group of students]] who went into hiding in the [[Plett's House|enclave]] of the [[Ho'Din/Legends|Ho'Din]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Plett]], which was located on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Belsavis/Legends|Belsavis]]. [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], however, discovered the group, and in [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]] he commissioned the colossal [[Battleship/Legends|dreadnought]] ''[[Eye of Palpatine]]'' to destroy them. When the [[Starship/Legends|vessel]] failed to arrive because of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Saboteur/Legends|sabotage]], Palpatine sent a backup force of [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] to finish the task. The Jedi [[Attack on Belsavis|repelled]] the attack, but had to evacuate from Belsavis, taking separate paths.

Marr eventually became an [[Artificial intelligence/Legends|artificial intelligence]] programmer at the [[Magrody Institute of Programmable Intelligence/Legends|Magrody Institute]] and fell in love with his colleague, [[Cray Mingla]]. The two joined Jedi Master [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker's]] [[Jedi Praxeum]] on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] in [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]], where Marr trained for about a [[12 ABY/Legends|year]] before being struck with a fatal disease, [[Quannot's Syndrome]]. Mingla tried to save his life by transferring Marr's consciousness into a [[Droid/Legends|droid]] body using [[Ssi-ruu]]k [[Entechment|technology]], but she was unable to do so, as the [[Nichos Marr (droid)|droid Marr]] turned out to be just that&mdash;a droid, while the real Marr had [[Death/Legends|died]]. Willing to rejoin Marr in the afterlife, Mingla later sacrificed her life to destroy the reactivated ''Eye of Palpatine'' and save Belsavis from its impending attack.

==Biography==
{{Quote|There's got to be something I can do.|Cray Mingla, after finding out about Marr's diagnosis|<ref name="COJ" />}}
Born at some point before [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]],<ref name="Age" /> Nichos Marr was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]]<ref name="EGT" /> [[Jedi Initiate/Legends|Jedi trainee]] at the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] during the waning days of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="NEGT" /> After the Republic was [[Declaration of a New Order|reformed]] into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]] began, Marr was among a [[Children of the Jedi|group of Jedi children]] who fled to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Belsavis/Legends|Belsavis]] and found refuge with the [[Ho'Din/Legends|Ho'Din]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Plett]] in his compound, which consisted of a [[Plett's House|house]] and a series of underground tunnels. On Belsavis, Marr and the other [[Youngling/Legends|children]] were cared for by the Ho'Din [[Brigantes Ustu]] and a young woman named [[Margolis Mingla]]. Plett also took precautions to protect the children, shielding a number of tunnels with mental barriers that induced dread in those that approached, and warning the children to stay away from the tunnels because of the dangerous [[Kretch insect]]s that lived there. Marr and other children, including [[Lagan Ismaren]] and [[Hoddas Umgil]], often played in the compound, daring each other to go to the forbidden tunnels to search for the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Plett's Well]].<ref name="COJ" />

[[File:Belsavis-TOR.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Belsavis, the planet where Marr was raised]]
In [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]],<ref name="Eye creation">According to [[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']], ''[[Eye of Palpatine]]'' was created thirty [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the events of the novel, which is dated to [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]] by ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''.</ref> [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] commissioned the massive [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]]-shaped [[Battleship/Legends|dreadnought]] ''[[Eye of Palpatine]]'' to wipe out the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] community on Belsavis, but the [[Starship/Legends|ship]] failed to arrive, having been [[Saboteur/Legends|sabotaged]] in the [[Moonflower Nebula/Legends|Moonflower Nebula]] by the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Callista Ming|Callista]]. In response, Palpatine ordered a backup [[Fighter wing/Legends|wing]] of [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] to [[Attack on Belsavis|destroy]] Plett's enclave. The Jedi defeated the Imperials by using [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|Y-wings]] and then left Belsavis, erasing the memory of their presence from the local [[Mluki]]s' minds and going separate ways. Remembering little from his childhood on Belsavis, Marr went on to become one of the most brilliant [[Artificial intelligence/Legends|artificial intelligence]] programmers at the [[Magrody Institute of Programmable Intelligence/Legends|Magrody Institute of Programmable Intelligence]]. At the institute, he met and fell in love with a fellow [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]], [[Cray Mingla]]; unbeknownst to Marr, she was the daughter of Margolis Mingla, who had taken care of him on Belsavis. Soon enough, the two became [[Marriage/Legends|engaged]].<ref name="COJ" /> In [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]],<ref name="Arrival date">According to [[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']], Marr arrived at the [[Jedi Praxeum]] a [[Standard year/Legends|year]] before the events of the novel, which ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates to [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]].</ref> Marr sought to be tested for [[Force-sensitive/Legends|sensitivity]] to [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], and arrived at Jedi Master [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker's]] newly established [[Jedi Praxeum]] on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]], accompanied by Mingla. Skywalker confirmed that they both were Force-sensitive, and the two started [[Jedi training/Legends|training]] at the Praxeum.<ref name="COJ" />

Marr was not the most powerful of Skywalker's students, but he proved himself to be a very steadfast learner and one that Skywalker was proud of. When Marr tried to [[Telekinesis/Legends|maneuver]] an edged weapon with the Force for the first time at the Academy, he failed, and the weapon left a scar on the little finger of his right hand. Marr trained for about a [[12 ABY/Legends|year]] at Skywalker's Academy until he was diagnosed with the fatal [[Quannot's Syndrome]], an inexplicable degenerative decay of the nervous system. Mingla spent many nights on Yavin researching, looking for a way to save her lover. As Marr was hospitalized on Coruscant and his life quickly faded away, Mingla decided to try to use forbidden [[Ssi-ruu]]k [[entechment]] technology to transfer Marr's life energy into a [[Droid/Legends|droid]] body. She personally designed a droid carcass to house Marr's essence, while the [[Technician/Legends|technicians]] of the [[biomedical institute]] on Coruscant replicated Marr's face and [[Limb/Legends|hands]] to the tiniest detail&mdash;complete with the scar and a [[birthmark]] on his right hand&mdash;creating prostheses which fitted perfectly into the droid body. Soon, Mingla performed the entechment procedure. The droid came to life and was seemingly indistinguishable from the real Marr, leading Mingla to believe that she had succeeded and had saved her fiancé from certain [[Death/Legends|death]].<ref name="COJ" />

In reality, the transfer had not worked as planned&mdash;the real Marr had succumbed to the disease and died during the procedure, while the [[Nichos Marr (droid)|droid]] turned out to be nothing more than a machine programmed with Marr's memories and mannerisms. When Mingla realized this aboard the reactivated ''Eye of Palpatine'' six [[Standard month/Legends|months]] later, she decided to sacrifice her life in order to destroy the dreadnought&mdash;which was due to arrive at Belsavis and attack Plett's Well&mdash;and to be reunited with her lover in death. Mingla exchanged places with Callista, whose essence had been trapped in the ''Eye''{{'s}} [[Computer/Legends|computer]] for many [[Standard year/Legends|years]]. Callista [[Essence transfer|transferred her spirit]] into Mingla's body and escaped from the dreadnaught, while Mingla occupied the computer and destroyed the ship with the droid Marr's help; both perished in the explosion.<ref name="COJ" /> By [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], Skywalker had established gray memorial plinths in a grove on Yavin IV, one for each of his deceased students, including Marr.<ref name="Dark Tide">''[[The New Jedi Order: Dark Tide I: Onslaught]]''</ref>

==Personality and traits==
Nichos Marr possessed great knowledge in the area of artificial intelligence and was considered one of the Magrody Institute's best specialists in that area. As a Jedi, he was determined to use the Force responsibly and correctly, and he spent a lot of [[Time/Legends|time]] in training. Marr deeply loved Cray Mingla, and she returned those feelings, going to great lengths to try to save Marr's life. Marr had [[Color/Legends|blue]] [[Eye/Legends|eyes]].<ref name="COJ" />

==Powers and abilities==
Nichos Marr was not very adept at using the Force, but Luke Skywalker respected his determination to learn. Marr's first attempt at using telekinesis resulted in him receiving the scar on his right hand.<ref name="COJ" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[Barbara Hambly]] created Nichos Marr for her [[1995]] novel [[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']].<ref name="COJ" /> Marr later received an entry along with his first visual depiction in ''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]''<ref name="EGT" /> and was briefly mentioned in several other novels and reference books. In ''Children of the Jedi'', Marr appears in his droid form, and the question of whether he is a man or a machine is raised throughout the novel numerous times, until in the end it is finally established that Marr is, in fact, a droid. Due to this revelation, the real Marr never actually appears in ''Children of the Jedi'', but is rather only mentioned by other characters.<ref name="COJ" /> Some sources, such as ''[[The New Jedi Order: Force Heretic II: Refugee]]''<ref name="Refugee">''[[The New Jedi Order: Force Heretic II: Refugee]]''</ref> and ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', however, still erroneously imply that the real Marr and the droid were the same person.<ref name="CSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> The eponymous Children of the Jedi in Hambly's novel were originally thought to be offspring of Jedi Knights of the Galactic Republic. However, with the release of the [[prequel trilogy]] and its ban on Jedi marriage, this has been [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]], with ''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'' establishing that they were trainees from the Jedi Temple on Coruscant.<ref name="NEGT" />
